rows.statement: The receiver of a frame it cannot apply answers with a refusal naming the frame hash, the first refused tx and the fault tag; the proposer, whose frame is pending and unacked, takes it back and, by the tag, either retries every tx at the next attempt (a fault that passes with the peer's view of J: an expiry not yet due, a lock too far ahead; at most MAX_ATTEMPTS retries per head, then a retryable fault is dropped like any other and the attempt keeps counting) or drops the refused tx with notice and re-proposes the rest; a refusal for a committed frame, or one whose index is not a tx of the frame, is ignored; Left wins simultaneous proposals. A frame carries its attempt number, the refusals its proposer has handled on this head. The receiver remembers one number per head, the highest attempt it refused, and refuses any frame at or below it without a look, answering with the refusal and the mark: a frame once refused is never committed later however its view of J moves (else the proposer, which took it back, and the peer would fork), and a retry, at a higher attempt, is judged afresh. The receiver judges any whole attempt number it can count, so a proposer past its retry budget is never ignored. The attempt count and that memory are Replica state: a Runtime that restarts must persist them. The Account has no clock: spacing the retries (propose again when a view of J moves, not back to back) is the Runtime's duty. The memory and the refusals are keyed by what a frame says, so they rest on the peer being authenticated: the transport authenticates it today, and A4b's signed frames and refusals, checked before the memory is consulted, take over. Without refusals a frame the peer refuses (an honest case: a deadline passing in flight) is stuck for good and a stuck Left frame blocks Right.
rows.source: coordinator 10-01 01:03 on Review A of PR 82 (F2), contracts-decisions.md Account-layer decisions

rows.statement: A frame of the peer's at my head that I do not judge afresh is answered with a refusal that names it and carries my mark for this head (the highest attempt I refused), never with silence: a frame that does not apply, a repeat of the frame I refused (the same frame, and only it, gets the same index and fault again), and any other frame at or below my mark (the fault stale_attempt, index 0) all get one. A stale answer judged nothing, so it costs the proposer no tx and no retry budget, and its next attempt is above the mark, so a proposer whose attempt count is behind (a restart that dropped it) catches up in one round trip and is never left pending, whatever frame it sends. A mark is trusted only while the proposer's next attempt stays a safe integer; a forged mark can wedge the proposer, as withholding acks can, and signed refusals (A4b) are the remedy. Silent on purpose, because there is no honest proposer to tell or nothing to take back: my own frame, an empty frame, a frame whose attempt is not a countable number, and a frame not at my head (R-REACK answers the one at my head with its ack).
rows.source: coordinator 10-01 02:52 on Review A of PR 85 (N1, N2)

rows.statement: An all-or-nothing order trades whole or is refused with the lots it could fill, and the book is unchanged.

rows.statement: A hub book holds at most maxOrders offers and an owner at most maxPerOwner; only an order that may rest needs room, and a cancel frees it.
rows.source: Hub matching engine thread, coordinator brief 10-01 02:56 (Arthur: the matching engine is a parallel job; the swap clause stays the Account's)

rows.statement: Every party that trades gets one execution: its Account moves by what it gave and got, and its swap clause is rebuilt from the lots still open at the offer's own price (or dropped when filled or withdrawn), never subtracted.
rows.source: Hub matching engine thread, coordinator brief 10-01 02:56 (Arthur: the matching engine is a parallel job; the swap clause stays the Account's)
